repetitive deformation stimulates Caco-2 cell motility across fibro-nectin in a manner involving Src activation and a FAK-Tyr925-dependent pathway that is Src independent.

repetitive mechanical strain activates a novel Src-independent, FAK-dependent pathway that activates the motogenic ERK in intestinal epithelial cells, and that this pathway may be an attractive target for interventions to improve mucosal healing.

repetitive deformation due to villi motility or perisitalsis may support intestinal mucosa and stimulate intestinal epithelial proliferation, and that cyclic strain enhances Caco2 and IEC6 intestinal epithelial cells migration across fibronetion via ERK.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of mechanical strain on epithelial cells and their ability to migrate across fibronectins in the intestinal mucosa.
the role of repetitive deformation in the intestinal mucosa in promoting intestinal epithelial restitution and proliferation.
the effects of mechanical forces on the intestinal mucosa and its ability to repair itself.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
repetitive deformation activates Src-independent, FAK-dependent ERKErk1/2 motogenic signals in Caco-2 epithelial cells.
repetitive deformation activates Src and FAK-dependent ERk motogenic signals in the intestinal epithelium, which may be important for intestinal homeostasis and repair.
repetitive deformation stimulates Caco-2 motility in a manner that is dependent on Src activation and a Src-independent FAK-mediated pathway that activates ERKI/II.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

repetitive mechanical deformation of the intestinal epithelium in a physiologic manner can activate a Src- and FAK-dependent ERKI/2 motogenic signaling pathway that promotes migration across the tissue fibronectins in the intestinal submucosa.
repetitive deformation due to villus motility and peristalsis activates Src-dependent and -independent FAK-dependent ERKI/2 motogenic signaling in human intestinal epithelial Caco-2 cells.
repetitive strain induces intestinal epithelial motogenic signals via FAK and ERK.
The main takeaway from our work is that

repetitive deformation activates Src-dependent FAK-dependent ERKI/II motogenic signals in Caco-2 human intestinal epithelial cells, and this pathway is important for the restitution of intestinal epithelial wounds.
repetitive strain activates a FAK-dependent ERKI/2 pathway in intestinal epithelial cells that promotes cell migration.
repetitive mechanical deformation of intestinal epithelial cells activates Src-dependent and Src-independent FAK-ERK motogenic signals that promote epithelial cell migration.
